$comment: The clause map of the Primmel conformance suite. Every clause states one conformance rule of the language; every case in corpus/cases.json names the clause it proves. The runner enforces the structural invariant: each clause carries at least one positive and one negative case. The 'spec' block names the document these clauses will re-key to when the Primmel Language Specification (TODO.standards/01) publishes its conformance clauses; until then the suite's own identifiers are the stable handles. Area anchors anticipate the specification's clause numbering without claiming it.

spec.status: MN 114, draft for comment (2026-08-28 revision, specifying Primmel v3.1)
spec.mapping: When the specification publishes, each clause's specAnchor is replaced by the specification's conformance-clause number. The suite identifiers (SYN-01, ..., CON-09) never change; only the anchor is re-keyed, in a minor suite release. The v3.1 clauses (DAT-01 to DAT-04) already anchor to MN 114 clause 19; the v3.2 clauses (CON-01 to CON-09) anchor to the MN 114 v3.2 clauses.

clauses.title: Document structure
clauses.statement: A Primmel document is a sequence of whitespace-delimited tokens forming (keyword, identifier, payload) triples; the header carries root, version, and the metadata block. A strict parse rejects an unknown top-level keyword; a lenient parse skips it.

clauses.title: Identifiers
clauses.statement: A construct keyword that takes an identifier consumes exactly one id token, bare or double-quoted; a quoted identifier may embed spaces and is referenced in the same quoted form. The id token is mandatory.

clauses.title: The requirement entity
clauses.statement: The requirement entity is declared as provision (narrative condition plus modality) or requirement (name, statement, modality, bindings); both spellings belong to the requirement kind. A value-taking keyword inside the body must carry its value.

clauses.title: The conformance test entity
clauses.statement: The conformance_test entity declares a name, an optional type, targets referencing declared requirements, a numbered procedure, and validation measurements. A value-taking keyword inside the body must carry its value.

clauses.title: The form entity
clauses.statement: The form entity declares a name and a set of fields, each field optionally carrying label, hint, and a bind path. A value-taking keyword inside the body must carry its value.

clauses.title: The calculation entity
clauses.statement: The calculation entity declares a name and an expression over bracketed quantity references. A value-taking keyword inside the body must carry its value.

clauses.title: The table entity
clauses.statement: The table entity declares a name, a column list, and rows keyed by row id with one value per column. A value-taking keyword inside the body must carry its value.

clauses.title: Re-serialization fixed point
clauses.statement: Serializing a parsed document and parsing the serialization again yields a model whose serialization is byte-identical: dump(parse(dump(parse(d)))) equals dump(parse(d)) for every valid document d. A document that fails to parse has no serialization.

clauses.title: Canonical emission
clauses.statement: The serializer emits one canonical form: the metadata block first, constructs in the language's declaration order, strings with embedded quotes and backslashes escaped. A document in canonical form serializes to itself byte-for-byte; a document in any other order does not serialize to its own input text.

clauses.title: Attribute bind scope
clauses.statement: A form field's bind path names a declared attribute definition whose scope matches the path's scope prefix.

clauses.title: Reference targets resolve
clauses.statement: Every cross-reference in the model (a conformance test's targets, a form's process link, a capability's satisfactions) resolves to a declared element.

clauses.title: Store uniqueness
clauses.statement: No two storable classes claim the same store.

clauses.title: Process flow integrity
clauses.statement: An executable process carries exactly one start event, and every flow edge begins and ends at a declared step.

clauses.title: Duplicate identification
clauses.statement: An identifier is declared at most once per id-keyed collection; a redeclaration is reported.

clauses.title: State machine initial
clauses.statement: A state machine declares its initial state — the starting state for new entities is required, so a machine without one is flagged; the serializer never emits the keyword without its value.

clauses.title: The package manifest
clauses.statement: A package is a directory whose package.primmel manifest declares at least the package id; the enumerated manifest facets (kind, status) carry only their declared values.

clauses.title: The edition register
clauses.statement: A package whose status is current or preview packages the edition register's newest entry.

clauses.title: Definition version pins
clauses.statement: An instance's definition_versions pins resolve against the package's edition register.

clauses.title: Layered composition
clauses.statement: A package's uses edges resolve against a package locator, never redefine an upstream identifier, and never form a cycle.

clauses.title: Abstract import pins
clauses.statement: A uses edge to a product reference package carries a version pin (id@edition), and the pin resolves against the product package's edition register.

clauses.title: Structural parse errors
clauses.statement: A structurally malformed document is rejected with an error that names the construct, the identifier where one exists, and the expected token.

clauses.title: Enumerated facet values
clauses.statement: A facet whose values are enumerated rejects an undeclared value with an error naming the valid set.

clauses.title: Duplicate identifier detection
clauses.statement: A document that redeclares an identifier parses with a duplicate-id issue on the issues channel.

clauses.title: The dataspace construct
clauses.statement: A dataspace declares its participant classes, its artifact classes (each optionally naming its content element and per-class policy override), the policy register, the default policy, the trust anchors, the compatibility register, and the governance citations. The policy register, the default policy, the per-class overrides, the content elements, and the compatibility register resolve (C104); the governance citations are present (C106, a warning).

clauses.title: The policy construct
clauses.statement: A policy declares rules of kind permission, obligation, or prohibition (a closed, parse-enforced vocabulary) over the dataspace's artifact classes and their actions, with constraints in the embedded expression dialect; default_posture is a closed parse-enforced boolean. A policy declares at least one rule, every rule carries its action, a rule's artifact stays inside the governs register, the governed classes resolve, and at most one default-posture policy governs a class (C107).

clauses.title: Trust references
clauses.statement: A trust_ref names an organization by its registry identifier, optionally with one published key by key id. The reference is opaque to the model: it carries addressing only, the consumer resolves it at runtime, and a conforming checker never resolves it — an organization no package declares is not a finding. The checker verifies the anchor's shape only (C105).

clauses.title: Correspondence annotations
clauses.statement: A corresponds facet declares an element's correspondence to an external concept (scheme token plus opaque concept identifier) with optional projection-steering blocks for the expression codecs; the facet is accepted on every construct (the multi-token skip discipline) and recorded on the projection-bearing kinds. One element carries at most one correspondence per scheme, an entry names its scheme and concept, and the irdi legacy spelling agrees with corresponds iec-cdd when both are present (C108).

clauses.title: The browser runtime surface
clauses.statement: The toolchain's browser-facing runtime module exposes the language's enumerated vocabularies as data — the passport content classes, access classes, and UPI levels, and the endpoint operation kinds and access scopes — so browser consumers read them from the toolchain and never re-declare them. A probe name the surface does not carry is reported absent, never rubber-stamped present.
clauses.specAnchor: the browser runtime surface (the reference toolchain's distribution)

clauses.title: The term alias family
clauses.statement: A term declares its everyday-words → defined-term bridge as the alias family (aliases, colloquial, abbreviations, deprecated, with spelling-tagged variant lists). Duplicate entries within one list of one term are errors (C110).

clauses.title: The dimension declaration
clauses.statement: A top-level dimension declares the applicability axis's value domain — values or values_of, never both; value identifiers are unique, every implies target resolves inside its own dimension, and the implication graph is acyclic (C111).

clauses.title: The structured reference identity
clauses.statement: A reference carries a resolvable identity: the urn facet, where present, is a well-formed IRI — a scheme followed by no whitespace or IRI delimiters (C112).

clauses.title: Edition lineage coherence
clauses.statement: A manifest's superseded_by forward edge, where declared, agrees with the successor's backward supersedes/replaces edges across the composed closure — opposite lineage edges between the same pair must agree; a missing forward edge is never an error (C113).

clauses.title: Limit quantity coherence
clauses.statement: A limit that declares its derived quantity's typing (quantity kind and unit) and binds a verdict agrees with the verdict's declared quantity, so a limit and its acceptance chain never drift apart in units (C114).

clauses.title: The calculation signature
clauses.statement: A calculation's declared quantity_kind resolves to a registered kind of the merged quantity register and agrees in kind with the declared unit (C115).

clauses.title: Verdict inputs resolve
clauses.statement: A verdict's inputs name the free identifiers of its derivation; every input resolves to a declared symbol, a conformance-test variable or observable, or another verdict (C116).

clauses.title: The verdict chain is acyclic
clauses.statement: An input naming another verdict makes the acceptance chain an explicit graph; the verdict→verdict derivation graph never cycles — a consumption system traverses the chain, and a cycle never terminates (C117).

clauses.title: The instance-parameter schema
clauses.statement: A requirement parameter's bind path names the aspect the value instantiates from and resolves against the subject's declared attribute, dimension, or behavior catalog (C118).
